source_text: Trapirionem itaque Apostolorum in toto mundo manifestatam, in omni Ecclesia adest perspicere omnibus qui vera velint videre, et habemus annumerare eos qui ab Apostolis instituti sunt Episcopi in ecclesiis, et successiones eorum usque ad nos, qui nihil tale docuerunt, neque cognoverunt, quale ab his deliratur. Etenim si recondita mysteria scissent Apostoli, que seorsim et latenter ab reliquis perfectos docebant, his vel maxime traderent ea quibus etiam ipsas ecclesias committebant. Valde enim fectos et irreprehensibiles in omnibus eos volebant esse, quos et successores relinquebant, suum ipsorum locum magisterii tradenemendate agentibus fieret magna utilitas, lapsis autem summa calamitas, Sed quoniam valde longum est, in hoe tali volumine omnium ecclesiarum enumerare successiones, maximz, et antiquissimz, et omnibus cognitz, a gloriosissimis duobus Apostolis ?
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the plan of the Apostles made manifest in the whole world, in every Church is present to be seen by all who wish to see the truth, and we have to count those who were instituted by the Apostles as Bishops in the churches, and their successions up to us, who taught nothing of the kind, nor knew it, such as is raved by these. For if the Apostles had known recondite mysteries, which they taught separately and secretly to the perfect, they would have handed them over especially to those to whom they also entrusted the churches themselves. For they wanted them to be very strong and irreprehensible in all things, whom they left as successors, so that a great benefit would be done to those who acted as teachers in their place, but the greatest calamity to those who fell. But since it is very long to enumerate in this kind of volume the successions of all the churches, and the greatest, and the most ancient, and known to all, from the two most glorious Apostles?
pass_b_english: The Apostles' plan has been made manifest throughout the whole world, and in every Church it is present to be seen by all who wish to see the truth. We are able to count those who were instituted by the Apostles as bishops in the churches, and their successions down to us — men who taught nothing of the kind, nor knew it, such as is raved by these heretics. For if the Apostles had known hidden mysteries, which they taught separately and secretly to the perfect, they would have handed them over especially to those to whom they also entrusted the churches themselves. They wanted those whom they left as successors to be very strong and irreproachable in all things, so that great benefit would come to those who acted as teachers in their place, but the greatest calamity to those who fell. But since it is very long to enumerate in a work of this kind the successions of all the churches, the greatest and most ancient and known to all, from the two most glorious Apostles?
